As a Public Health student and future nurse, I am deeply concerned about how the weakening of environmental safeguards in federal oil and gas leasing—specifically the removal of mitigation measures not included in approved Resource Management Plans (RMPs)—may negatively impact community and environmental health.

This change could significantly limit the Bureau’s ability to address new environmental, public health, and tribal concerns that emerge after RMPs are finalized. Oil and gas development has been shown to release pollutants that increase risks of asthma, cardiovascular disease, and birth complications in nearby communities. Without flexibility to include site-specific stipulations or updates, we risk exposing vulnerable populations, including tribal and rural residents, to long-term harm.

While I understand this rule aligns with the statutory language in the “One Big Beautiful Bill Act,” I urge BLM to ensure that RMPs are frequently reviewed and updated with robust public input, including from health professionals, environmental scientists, and Indigenous leaders. Public health must be a core consideration in land management decisions.

Thank you for the opportunity to comment.

Revision to Regulations Regarding Oil and Gas Leasing; Stipulations and Information Notices Direct Final Rule (Docket No. BLM-2025-0140)



Dear Principal Deputy Director Groffy,



On behalf of all of our youth clients, including our clients in Lighthiser v. Trump and Genesis v. EPA, and on behalf of America’s children and youth, Our Children’s Trust provides these comments on the “Revision to Regulations Regarding Oil and Gas Leasing; Stipulations and Information Notices” direct final rule to remove existing BLM regulations pertaining to oil and gas leasing on Federal lands to effectuate changes required by the “One Big Beautiful Bill Act”.



As the Nation’s only law firm dedicated to representing children and youth whose constitutional rights are being infringed by government conduct that causes and contributes to climate change, we write to advise you that your rulemaking must be consistent with protecting the rights to life, personal security, other liberties of young people, and children’s equal protection of the law. U.S. Const. amend. V, XIV, § 1. We seek to advise you on behalf of our clients that your regulatory proposal is inconsistent with the federal law, the best available science on protecting the health and lives of children, and the legal mandate that agency decision-making does not deprive children of their fundamental constitutional rights, including explicit and recognized rights to life; liberty; property; personal security; family autonomy; bodily integrity; the practice and transmission of cultural and religious traditions; and equal protection of the law.

PLEASE SEE ATTACHED COMMENT.

Sincerely,



/s/

Julia Olson

Co-executive Director and Chief Legal Counsel

julia@ourchildrenstrust.org



Our Children’s Trust

P.O. Box 5181

Eugene, OR 97405
